title: What an idle activity would need to earn

blocks.text: A school district's facilities office solves an LP each spring to split its repair money. Every year some kinds of work get nothing, and their sponsors ask the same question: "how much better would our work have to be to get funded?" The office wants the answer for every unfunded kind of work, from one solve.

For an LP solved to optimality, a variable $`x_j`$ that the plan leaves at 0 has reduced cost $`d_j`$ (MathOpt's `result.reduced_costs(var)`). Its **entry value**, the objective coefficient at which it starts to pay, is

where $`c_j`$ is its coefficient in the objective (`model.objective.get_linear_coefficient(var)`). The formula holds for a maximization ($`d_j \le 0`$, so the entry value is above $`c_j`$) and for a minimization ($`d_j \ge 0`$, so it is below).

Write `entry_values(model, tol=1e-9)` in `entry.py`. Solve `model` with GLOP. If the solve does not end `OPTIMAL`, return `{}`. Otherwise return a dict mapping the name of every variable whose value is within `tol` of 0 to its entry value; variables in use do not appear.

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

from entry import entry_values

# A council's road money ($k): value per $k of each kind of work.
model = mathopt.Model(name="roads")
x = {name: model.add_variable(lb=0, name=name) for name in ("potholes", "resurface", "signs", "lines")}
model.add_linear_constraint(sum(x.values()) <= 80, name="budget")
model.add_linear_constraint(x["potholes"] <= 30, name="pothole_crews")
model.maximize(0.9 * x["potholes"] + 0.7 * x["resurface"] + 0.4 * x["signs"] + 0.1 * x["lines"])

for name, value in entry_values(model).items():
    print(f"entry value of {name}:", round(value, 4))

cases.says: an idle activity's entry value is its coefficient less its reduced cost, and above it the activity enters the plan
only the variables the optimal plan leaves at 0 are reported
in a minimization the idle variable's reduced cost is positive, and its cost must fall below its entry value

origin.section: A Reduced Cost Is the Price of Forcing an Idle Variable Into the Plan

concepts: MathOpt's dual_values and reduced_costs are the change in the objective as written, per unit of a row's or a variable's bound
an idle variable's reduced cost is the cost of forcing it in, and its coefficient must pass c minus d before it enters
